birth.place: Smithtown, Suffolk County, New York, USA

summary: John's 8th-great-grandfather; son of Job Smith and grandson of Bull Smith, he held land on the edge of the Hauppauge estate and settled in Moriches.
bio: Son of Job Smith 1st & Elizabeth Thompson. In Smithtown in the mid-1720s; his earmark was recorded in 1725 (Pelletreau pp. 82–83). In the 1736 General Division he drew 152 acres 'on the east side of Smithtown river, near the northeast branch,' bounded south by land laid out to Daniel Smith (pp. 311–312); a tract of his first cousin Daniel Smith 2d's 'at the head of the Northeast Branch, bounded south by Islip line' was bounded north 'by James Smith's land' (p. 361) — the closest John's direct line comes to Hauppauge. He then sold shares to his brothers (pp. 297, 398–400) and 'settled in Moriches' on the Brookhaven south shore (App. p. 479). Married Jerusha Topping, daughter of Elnathan & Mary Topping. Children per Pelletreau: Matthew (b. 1721), Ezekiel, Zebulon, Austin, Nathaniel, Francis, Eunice, Keturah, Temperance, Jeremiah. Sons Austin, Francis and Jeremiah went to Orange County (Capts. Austin and Francis Smith; Jeremiah Smith's will 1776/1783). No NY will for James (d. 1740) was found; no Smith will in the Smith Wills volume names Temperance. TREE vs PDF: the tree (and an earlier screenshot version of the chart) shows his father as 'Justice, A Smith' / 'Justice Adam Smith 1649–1726'; the uploaded Bull Smith PDF shows Job Smith + Elizabeth Thompson c.1647–c.1719. Preferred: Job (upload overrides tree; F. K. Smith 'James Smith (Job, Richard)'). Do not confuse with the Hauppauge James Smith (d. 1837 aged 95) from Lake Ronkonkoma, who married Catherine Blydenburgh — a different, non-Bull family.
